From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Semantic embeddings — fit recommendations & opportunity map (Brightline Health)

Hi Sasha / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a recommended path to validate model fit for your semantic search use cases (clinical triage + patient-facing KB). I kept the notes short and included concrete next steps so we can get a POC running next week.

High-level fit assessment from call:
- Corpus: mixed clinical notes (~70%), product/marketing pages (~20%), patient FAQs (~10%).
- Primary success metrics you called out: recall@10 for diagnosis lookup, MRR for clinician-assisted triage, and clustering purity for topic grouping.
- Concerns: drift on free-text clinician notes, short-text query ambiguity, and PHI handling for notes ingestion.

Recommended models to try (start small, then scale):
1) RWI-Embed-Base-v2 (256d) — Redwood-verified, low-latency, strong recall on short clinical queries; good baseline for production.
2) OpenEmbed/768-large — higher-dimensional candidate for improving MRR on long-context passages (expect higher costs).
3) RWI-Embed-Quant8-512 — quantized variant to test unit-cost reduction while monitoring quality regressions.

Key evaluation artifacts we should run:
- Benchmark: recall@1/5/10, MRR, average intra-doc cosine variance, embedding norm distribution, and nearest-neighbor type confusion (clinical vs marketing).
- Prompt/Query set: 500 seeded queries derived from triage flows + 1k random queries for stability. Attached: brightline_eval_promptset_v1.jsonl (starter).
- Samples: initial run on 5k documents (stratified across note types) then expand to 50k if early signals are promising.

Preliminary guardrails for drift/regression:
- Baseline snapshot: store RWI-Embed-Base-v2 vectors for the initial 5k sample and compute monthly drift via centroid cosine shift + fraction of tokens with >0.2 norm delta.
- Alerting: if recall@10 drops >6% vs baseline or MRR drops >8%, trigger regression workflow.

Operational asks from Brightline:
- Provide a 5k sample (S3 link or secure transfer) with metadata schema similar to brightline_sample_metadata_schema.csv.
- Confirm whether you want PHI redaction applied pre-ingest or whether we should run evaluation inside your VPC (we can do both; Marissa will propose the secure option).

Next steps / owners:
- Sasha: share sample by EOD Wed (S3 or SFTP) — required to start 5k run.
- Marissa: run the initial evaluation on Redwood Dedicated (config + cost estimate) and return results + embed_benchmark_results_stub.csv by Fri.
- Logan: coordinate evaluation notebook and meeting to review results the following week.

Attachments: starter prompt set, sample metadata schema.

Thanks — happy to jump on another quick call if helpful.

Best,

Logan Wright

On Tue, Jun 28, 2028 at 5:02 PM Sasha Green <sasha@brightlinehealth.com> wrote:
> Logan — thanks for the clear plan and the artifacts. A couple quick clarifying questions before we move samples: 
> 
> 1) For the 5k vs 50k split — what minimum sample distribution do you need across the three doc types?
> 2) On PHI redaction: we'd prefer to avoid shipping PHI to third-party services. Can you confirm Redwood can perform the evaluation entirely inside our VPC?

Hi Sasha —

We can absolutely run the initial evaluation inside Brightline's Private deployment (VPC) so PHI never leaves your environment. Operational notes: 
- Private eval adds ~1 business day for onboarding if we already have a VPC connector and permissions. If we need an on-prem appliance, add ~1 week.
- For a reliable first pass we recommend: 2,500 clinician notes, 1,500 product/marketing pages, 1,000 FAQs — totalling 5k stratified sample. That distribution gives signal across short queries and long passages.

Evaluation harness we will run (attached):
- embed_eval_runner.py (internal) run against the three model configs listed by Logan.
- Outputs: per-query nearest-neighbor lists, metric aggregates (MRR/Recall@k), and embedding distribution diagnostics.

Cost/time estimate:
- 5k run (3 models): ~6 compute-hours on a 16GB GPU cluster; expected turnaround 48 hours from sample arrival if run inside your VPC.
- 50k run: ~60 compute-hours; recommend after we validate the 5k signal.

I've attached a starter promptset and a results stub to show the expected CSV layout. I'll queue the Dedicated config and add a canary rollout to control for incidental regressions when we try the quantized variant.

If Sasha confirms the sample and VPC details I will:
- Provision eval job and S3 staging inside your VPC.
- Share a short notebook link with the visualization of embedding clusters and recall curves.

Marissa Cole
Principal Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

2) VPC: we'll run the eval inside your Private deployment per Marissa's notes (adds ~1 business day). We'll coordinate with your security team on temporary S3 staging + KMS key. I attached a short security summary (redwood-security-sla-summary.pdf) for your InfoSec.

- Tue 7/3: Sasha shares 5k sample (secure S3 link) or confirms VPC connector.
- Wed 7/4: Marissa kicks off 5k, runs three model configs, and posts initial results.
- Fri 7/6: 30-min sync to review results + decision on 50k expansion.
